A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same OmniBal study. Their text, equations, tables, and matching figure content support comparison, including the material reorganized into Appendices A-K in v4.

before.justification: v2 reports original training-time measurements, downstream benchmark scores, component ablations, convergence analyses, and GPU-scaling experiments.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results in the main text and Appendices B-K, including benchmark scores, GPU-day measurements, and scaling experiments.

M1.justification: The ISF sampling/filtering algorithm, partition-candidate search and ranking, and four-step adaptive recomputation procedure remain unchanged. Reorganization and additional overhead documentation do not establish a procedural change.

E1.justification: The same training datasets, downstream benchmarks, pretraining tasks, image-resolution scenarios, and Qwen2-VL preprocessing tests appear in both versions. v4's appendices relocate existing coverage, including LLaVA-665K, InternVL-1.2M, and LCS-558K.

E2.justification: Tables 2-4 retain the same comparisons: DeepSpeed and Megatron backends; random, length-group, and device-group batching; and parameter-, layer-, and profile-based partitioning. No evaluated comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: Reported datasets, metrics, model configurations, parallelism settings, and hardware configurations match. The Qv=9 and Qt=4K settings, five profiling steps, and three-step measurements of 10-15 candidate partitions are retained; Section 5.2 reorganizes their documentation.

E4.justification: Table 6 revises the existing threshold-sensitivity evidence: Qt-128 now has lower ViT DistRatio than Qt-64, reversing their previous ordering. The component ablations, convergence curves, and other sensitivity and scaling analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Table 1 retains its input, timing, and memory dispersion statistics. Neither version adds experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: In Table 6, ViT DistRatio changes from 0.0156 to 0.0159 for Qt-64 and from 0.0159 to 0.0156 for Qt-128. The PDFs do not explain this swap. Main benchmark scores, GPU-day results, convergence curves, and generalization results otherwise match.

T1.justification: v4 Section 5.2 adds the ISF time-complexity statement O(C·(N+M)), defining the iteration count, total sample count, and samples per pack. v2 has no corresponding asymptotic statement. No derivation is supplied, and Equations 1-5 remain unchanged.

C1.justification: Both versions claim to identify VLM computation imbalance and address it jointly through data, model, and memory balancing. The approximately 1.8× acceleration claim, preserved model performance, and broad generalizability claims retain their scope.

C2.justification: The explanations of imbalance, component complementarity, communication overhead, and LLaVA's smaller acceleration are retained. Moving these discussions does not change their interpretation. The new generic impact statement adds no substantive limitation or applicability boundary.

D1.justification: v4 newly specifies that sampling 1.2 million examples takes a few tens of seconds; v2 reports ten ISF iterations taking under one minute more generally. Existing hyperparameters, profiling instructions, hardware information, and the code-release location and promise are retained.

R1.justification: v4 adds a formal Qwen2-VL citation and bibliography entry attributed to the Qwen team, 2024. v2 already discusses and evaluates its preprocessing strategy. The broader related-work discussion and novelty positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v4 integrates Section 3's separate quantitative evidence into the corresponding imbalance explanations, creates a dedicated implementation subsection, and replaces detailed main-text generalization discussion with an appendix guide. Convergence and generalization material move into labeled appendices, alongside language and front-matter edits and new acknowledgements and impact statements.

P2.justification: Figures 3-4 and Tables 8-16 are substantially reorganized into appendices, with table renumbering, resizing, and a single-column appendix layout. Table 6 gains a caption above the table and emphasis on the selected setting. The four figures themselves retain their content.

improvement.justification: v4 improves navigation by pairing imbalance evidence with its explanations and organizing previously scattered results into labeled appendices; experimental tables no longer interrupt the references. The added ISF overhead documentation and Qwen2-VL citation provide modest transparency gains. The method and empirical foundation remain essentially unchanged, and the unexplained Table 6 swap does not establish better performance, so the overall improvement is limited.
